transcript.answer:
Agent pods run in a Kubernetes cluster as Agent CRs in the `ai-agents` namespace. The ai-agent-subsystem controller starts them, and its images live in the separate private repo re-cinq/ai-agent-subsystem. There can be more than one execution cluster, each with its own `cluster-agent`.

The Floor no longer holds a Kubernetes client for this, but Lore as a whole still does. ADR-044 extracted `apps/cluster-agent` as the only process holding a Kubernetes client, one per cluster. The Floor and other callers reach it over bearer-authed HTTP under `/api/cluster`, and it reports terminal Agent CR phases back through the event-router's `POST /api/events`. Earlier, the Floor held its own client (`@kubernetes/client-node`) and created Agent CRs directly. That was before the cluster-agent extraction, and ADR-044 itself still says the Floor holds one. One caveat: ADR-044 also says the event-router's watch only needs a kubeconfig, so it may still read a kubeconfig for observation. I did not confirm that.

judgements.reason: The answer claims Lore still holds a Kubernetes client via apps/cluster-agent and places pods in an ai-agent-subsystem cluster rather than the external floor reached through @re-cinq/floor-client.
